recommendation: Keep the no-change audit for the current FHIR source. If HL7 wants to repair the still-invalid R4B/R5 published expansions.json archives, handle that as release/archive publication maintenance or generator/data backport work outside this current-source reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-36244 was a Published/Persuasive R4B technical correction reporting that the ValueSet expansion download, especially expansions.json, contained thousands of designation entries without the required designation.value, mostly zh-CN.
initial_application: No explicit source commit tagged FHIR-36244 was found. The current source downloads page still exposes generated expansion downloads, and current build.fhir.org/R6 downloadable expansion outputs validate for the reported condition. However, the historical R4B and R5 published expansions.json artifacts still contain missing-value designations, indicating the archived release artifacts were not cleanly repaired by a traceable source commit.
additional_context: The only checked-in expansion artifacts are tools/history/release*/expansions.xml history snapshots; there is no checked-in root expansions.json/xml download to edit. The release4b and release5 history XML snapshots still mirror the historical missing-value data, but they are generated historical/version-diff inputs rather than the current build output. Zulip confirms the issue arose from R4B implementation testing, and Confluence searches found no separate decision changing that scope.
reconciliation: Published current build.fhir.org/expansions.json and hl7.fhir.r6.expansions.tgz were traversed and both had zero designation entries missing value, so the current spec source/output is already correct for the reported validation condition. No source hunk was applied because editing generated historical XML snapshots would not fix current downloadable output or archived R4B/R5 publication artifacts.
